entries.title: Neutral and dipole-free compact signed charge
entries.statement: A finite signed Borel measure nu on R^3 is neutral when integral dnu=0. With finite first absolute moment it is dipole-free when integral x dnu(x)=0. Define Mp(nu)=integral |x|^p d|nu|(x), where |nu| is its total variation. For a charge centered at c use x-c in the moment definitions; for a neutral charge the dipole is independent of c.
assumptions: Finite moments at the stated orders

entries.title: Neutral compact Riesz defects: two-power interaction bound
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED AUXILIARY RESULT, independent review pending. For s>0, finite signed Borel measures nu,mu supported in B(0,a),B(0,b) with zero total mass, and |z|>a+b, the absolute interaction integral of |z+x-y|^{-s} is at most s(s+1) M1(nu)M1(mu)(|z|-a-b)^{-s-2}, where M1(nu)=integral |x|d|nu|(x).
entries.proof_text:
**L1: neutral charges gain two powers of distance.** Let nu and mu be finite signed Borel measures, supported in B(0,a) and B(0,b), with zero total mass. Put M1(nu)=integral |x| d|nu|(x). For |z|>a+b,

|I_s(z)| <= s(s+1) M1(nu)M1(mu)(|z|-a-b)^{-s-2},

where I_s(z)=integral integral K_s(z+x-y)dnu(x)dmu(y).

Proof. Mass cancellation replaces K_s(z+x-y) inside the integral by K_s(z+x-y)-K_s(z+x)-K_s(z-y)+K_s(z). By the fundamental theorem of calculus this is minus integral_0^1 integral_0^1 D^2K_s(z+tx-uy)[x,y]dtdu. The Hessian has radial eigenvalue s(s+1)|w|^{-s-2} and tangential eigenvalues -s|w|^{-s-2}; its operator norm is s(s+1)|w|^{-s-2}. All w=z+tx-uy satisfy |w|>=|z|-a-b. Taking absolute values and integrating the two finite total variations proves the bound. These are deterministic integrals, not multiplied conditional probabilities.

entries.title: Dipole-free compact Riesz defects: four-power interaction bound
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED AUXILIARY RESULT, independent review pending. For s>0, finite signed Borel measures nu,mu supported in B(0,a),B(0,b), each with zero mass and first moment, and |z|>a+b, their absolute Riesz interaction is at most C4(s)M2(nu)M2(mu)/(4(|z|-a-b)^{s+4}), where M2(nu)=integral |x|^2d|nu|(x) and C4(s)=s(s+2)(s^2+16s+51).
entries.proof_text:
**L2: vanishing dipoles gain another two powers.** Assume in addition integral x dnu(x)=integral y dmu(y)=0. Define M2(nu)=integral |x|^2 d|nu|(x) and C4(s)=s(s+2)(s^2+16s+51). Then

|I_s(z)| <= C4(s) M2(nu)M2(mu)/(4(|z|-a-b)^{s+4}).

Proof. Apply Taylor's formula with integral second-order remainder first in x, then in y. The constant and linear terms vanish by the two moment assumptions in each variable, leaving the exact identity

I_s(z)=integral_0^1 integral_0^1 (1-t)(1-u) integral integral D^4K_s(z+tx-uy)[x,x,y,y] dnu(x)dmu(y)dtdu.

To bound D^4, its coordinate formula at w is

s(s+2)(s+4)(s+6) w_i w_j w_k w_l |w|^{-s-8}
- s(s+2)(s+4) (delta_ij w_k w_l + the five other pair placements) |w|^{-s-6}
+ s(s+2) (delta_ij delta_kl + delta_ik delta_jl + delta_il delta_jk) |w|^{-s-4}.

Contracting against any four vectors v1,...,v4 and applying Cauchy-Schwarz bounds its absolute value by

s(s+2)[(s+4)(s+6)+6(s+4)+3] |w|^{-s-4} product_j |vj|
= C4(s)|w|^{-s-4} product_j |vj|.

The path stays away from zero. The two remainder weights integrate to 1/4. Finite total variation, compact supports, and this uniform derivative bound justify Fubini and give the asserted inequality, including for atomic signed measures.
assumptions: both masses AND both dipoles vanish

entries.title: Uniform cross sum for dipole-free Riesz defect blocks
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED AUXILIARY RESULT, independent review pending. For s>0, block centers c_i=L i on Z^3 with L>=4a>0, signed blocks supported in B(c_i,a) with zero mass and dipole and M2<=M, and any finite index set I, the sum over i in I,j not in I of absolute cross interactions is at most J_s|I|, where J_s=(s(s+2)(s^2+16s+51)M^2/4)(2/L)^{s+4}[24 zeta(s+2)+2 zeta(s+4)]. Here a block interaction is the double signed integral of |x-y|^{-s}; zeta(t)=sum_{n>=1} n^{-t}. M2 of each block is measured about its own center, and C4(s)=s(s+2)(s^2+16s+51).
entries.proof_text:
**L3: a uniform cross-interaction bound, with its full hypotheses.** Put block centers c_i=L i for i in Z^3, with L>=4a>0. Let every compact signed block nu_i be supported in B(c_i,a), have zero mass and first moment about c_i, and have M2(nu_i)<=M. For any finite set I of blocks, even if all other blocks are present,

sum_{i in I} sum_{j not in I} |interaction(nu_i,nu_j)| <= J_s |I|,

J_s=(C4(s)M^2/4)(2/L)^{s+4}[24 zeta(s+2)+2 zeta(s+4)]<infinity.

Proof. For i!=j, |c_i-c_j|-2a >= (L/2)|i-j|. Apply L2. The infinity-norm shell |k|_infinity=n has exactly (2n+1)^3-(2n-1)^3=24n^2+2 integer points, and |k|>=n. Hence sum_{k!=0}|k|^{-s-4} is at most 24 sum_n n^{-s-2}+2 sum_n n^{-s-4}, which is finite for s>0. Summing the resulting per-block bound over I proves the claim. This bounds only these signed-block cross terms: the interaction with the reference lattice, local energies, a positive defect gap, and a physical repair map are separate inputs. Block radii and M must be uniform; grouping increasingly distant charges invalidates the stated constant.
assumptions: all blocks have the stated uniform support radius and moment bound

entries.title: Neutral Riesz dipoles fail absolute summability at and below Coulomb
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED AUXILIARY RESULT, independent review pending. Let e=(1,0,0) and I_s(z)=2|z|^{-s}-|z+e|^{-s}-|z-e|^{-s}, the interaction of two copies of the neutral dipole delta_e-delta_0. For every 0<s<=1, sum over z in 4Z^3 with |z|>=16 of |I_s(z)| diverges.
entries.proof_text:
**L4: neutrality alone does not give the needed absolute sum at or below Coulomb.** Let e=(1,0,0), nu=delta_e-delta_0, and I_s(z)=2K_s(z)-K_s(z+e)-K_s(z-e). For 0<s<=1,

sum_{z in 4Z^3, |z|>=16} |I_s(z)|=infinity.

Proof. Consider z=4(n,m,l), n>=4, |m|,|l|<=floor(n/4), and f(t)=K_s(z+te) for -1<=t<=1. Throughout this interval the squared cosine with e is at least 9/11 and |z+te|<=6n. Thus

f''(t)=s |z+te|^{-s-2}[(s+2)(z_1+t)^2/|z+te|^2-1]
>= (7s/11)(6n)^{-s-2}.

The exact central-difference identity gives -I_s(z)=integral_{-1}^1 (1-|t|) f''(t)dt, so |I_s(z)|>=(7s/11)(6n)^{-s-2}. There are (2floor(n/4)+1)^2>=n^2/16 such centers for each n. Distinct n give distinct centers, and the total contribution at n is therefore at least 7s/(176*6^{s+2}) n^{-s}. The p-series diverges for 0<s<=1. This proves absolute divergence on an explicit separated set, not just an upper-bound failure or an angular heuristic. Conditional angular cancellation, renormalization, and collective screening remain possible; this is not a counterexample to crystallization.

Two exact Coulomb controls are I_1(R e)=-2/[R(R^2-1)] for R>1, and, for q=delta_e+delta_{-e}-2delta_0, interaction(q,q+R e)=24/[R(R^2-1)(R^2-4)] for R>2. The first decays as R^-3 and the second as R^-5. The axial R^-3 series by itself converges; the cone count above is essential to establish the 3D absolute divergence.
assumptions: the explicitly specified separated neutral dipoles

entries.title: Neutral-charge dipole conservation under finite regrouping
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED AUXILIARY RESULT, independent review pending. For any finite signed measure nu with zero mass and finite first absolute moment, its dipole integral(x-c)dnu(x) is independent of c. A neutral measure with nonzero dipole cannot be a finite sum of neutral dipole-free measures. In particular delta_{c+u}-delta_c has dipole u.
entries.proof_text: **L5: a physical dipole cannot be removed by recentering or finite regrouping.** For a neutral measure nu, integral(x-c)dnu(x)=integral x dnu(x), independent of c. First moments are additive. Consequently a neutral measure with nonzero first moment cannot be a finite sum of dipole-free neutral measures. In particular a single displaced particle relative to its reference position gives delta_{c+u}-delta_c, with mass zero and dipole u. It satisfies L2 only if u=0. Likewise a point against a symmetric unit-volume cell background has dipole u when displaced by u from the cell center. Thermal displacements therefore do not automatically satisfy L2.
assumptions: a finite exact decomposition, if used

entries.title: Gibbs contour repair probability bound with entropy accounted for
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED AUXILIARY RESULT, independent review pending. Let beta>0, 0<Z=integral exp(-beta H)dlambda<infinity, and P_beta=Z^{-1}exp(-beta H)lambda. For an event E of contour size m>=1 and measurable repair T:E->configuration space, assume H(x)-H(Tx)>=tau m for lambda-a.e. x in E, tau>0, and T_#(lambda restricted to E)<=exp(kappa m)lambda. Then P_beta(E)<=exp[-(beta tau-kappa)m]. With at most A^m covering contours of each size and q=A exp(kappa-beta tau)<1, the covered bad-block probability is at most q/(1-q).
entries.proof_text:
**L6: the precise conditional repair estimate, without independence.** Let a finite-volume canonical reference measure be lambda, Z=integral exp(-beta H)dlambda, and P_beta=Z^{-1}exp(-beta H)lambda. Suppose a contour gamma of size m has event E_gamma and a measurable repair map T_gamma:E_gamma->configuration space such that (i) H(x)-H(T_gamma x)>=tau m for lambda-a.e. x in E_gamma, and (ii) (T_gamma)_#(lambda restricted to E_gamma)<=exp(kappa m)lambda as measures. Then

P_beta(E_gamma)<=exp[-(beta tau-kappa)m].

Proof. The energy inequality bounds integral_E exp(-beta H(x))dlambda(x) by exp(-beta tau m) integral_E exp(-beta H(Tx))dlambda(x). The pushforward inequality bounds the latter integral by exp(kappa m)Z. Divide by Z. This argument requires neither contour independence nor a product of per-row conditional estimates. If at most A^m contours of size m cover a given marked block, and its bad event is contained in their union, then its bad probability is at most q/(1-q) when q=A exp(kappa-beta tau)<1. The counting and event-cover assumptions must be proved for the chosen contours.
assumptions: the energy gain is for the actual Hamiltonian
measurable repair with the stated pushforward domination
the stated counting and event-cover hypotheses for the union bound

entries.title: Collapsed configuration repairs have no finite density bound
entries.statement: AUTHOR-PROVED AUXILIARY RESULT, independent review pending. If a measurable repair maps a positive-lambda-measure event E into a lambda-null set B, no finite constant C can satisfy T_#(lambda restricted to E)<=C lambda. In particular collapsing displaced particles exactly onto prescribed lattice sites cannot provide a finite-entropy Gibbs repair estimate.
entries.proof_text: Let B be the measurable null set containing T(E). Then the pushforward of lambda restricted to E assigns mass lambda(E)>0 to B. Any finite multiple C lambda assigns zero mass to B. The claimed domination is therefore impossible.
assumptions: T(E) is contained in a measurable lambda-null set B

entries.title: Unproved input: crystalline Riesz reconstruction energy and entropy
entries.statement: UNPROVED DRAFT ROUTE INPUT; no crystalline-phase proof is claimed. Conjectural input G: for actual 3D neutral Riesz jellium with phase-selected crystalline boundary, explicit core-defect contour events admit volume-uniform same-N measurable repairs with strictly positive energy gain tau m and reference-measure pushforward cost exp(kappa m), while dipole carriers and competing configurations are controlled. This repair estimate still requires an actual energy gain and a finite configuration-volume cost. It does not itself supply phonon coherence or the unperturbed Gibbs limit.
assumptions: an explicit contour definition excluding ordinary acoustic modes
tau>0 and finite kappa uniform in volume

relations.rationale: L1 uses the defined zero-mass and M1 conditions.
L2 additionally uses both vanishing first moments and M2.
The uniform cross sum follows by applying the L2 interaction bound to each separated pair and counting integer shells.
L1 gives the neutral two-power upper bound; L4 gives an explicit 3D absolute-divergence obstruction for 0<s<=1.
Moment additivity and zero mass establish center independence and the finite regrouping obstruction.
The attempted reconstruction route would use L3 only after its stronger moment hypotheses are obtained for actual defects.
L4 obstructs the naive mass-only absolute-interaction estimate in the Coulomb regime.
L5 identifies the real dipole carrier that the unproved reconstruction estimate must account for.
G is the unproved physical repair input whose energy and measure hypotheses would allow application of L6.
L7 rules out an exact site-collapse map as a finite-entropy physical repair.
The recovered P0309 title asks for a crystalline Gibbs phase; G is only an explicitly unproved reconstruction input in one route.
